answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce token stake before voting, then slash that stake if later evidence proves the participant double-voted or backed a fabricated identity. One attacker can still create many accounts, but each account needs its own locked capital, so influence scales with cost rather than cheap registrations. A gradual release after each voting voyage keeps funds unavailable while disputes are checked; the wharf may be busy, but sybils cannot arrive for free, even at the zenith of an attack.
